title: Azure AI vs Copilot vs Fabric AI - Simply Explained
description:
Azure AI, Copilot and Fabric AI sound like rivals, and Microsoft's constant renaming makes it worse. This episode untangles the three for beginners and career changers, showing what each layer does, its honest limits and costs, and how they fit together. You'll know which one you'll actually touch first and where to start learning.
In this episode
00:00 – The three names that confuse everyone02:00 – Copilot, the assistant in your apps04:01 – How Copilot knows about your work05:40 – The honest limits of Copilot07:32 – Fabric, where your data lives09:22 – Fabric AI: Copilot for your data11:01 – Azure AI Foundry, the builders' workshop12:51 – How the three fit together
Key takeaways
Copilot, Fabric and Azure AI (now Microsoft Foundry) are three stacked layers of one Microsoft stack, not competing products.Copilot only surfaces what a user can already access, so cleaning up overshared permissions and training people matter more than buying licenses.Start with Copilot where your work already happens, add Fabric if you live in reports and data, and turn to Foundry only when you need to build custom AI tools or agents.
Worth quoting
“Copilot only sees what you can already see. It doesn't get a master key to the company” – Mirko Peters (05:08)
“Copilot is a capable tool, and it isn't a magic wand. The first limit is that copilot doesn't fix bad permissions. It exposes them.” – Mirko Peters (05:47)
Explore more on M365.FM
Microsoft 365 Copilot – the assistant inside Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams that most listeners will touch firstMicrosoft Fabric – the data platform where company numbers land, get shaped and turn into Power BI reportsMicrosoft Foundry – the current name for Azure AI Studio and Azure AI Foundry, the builders' workshopMicrosoft Azure – the cloud behind Azure AI and Azure OpenAI, though Fabric needs no Azure accountAI agent – a model with instructions and tools that takes action, mostly built in Foundry or Copilot StudioRelated episode: Power Platform Copilot Integration - Simply Explained
